If a live channel has shown no picture by this time, KevBox Live stops trying and tells you, instead of leaving a black screen while it works through every player it has. Never keeps trying, which can take well over a minute on a channel your provider has removed. Waits your provider asks for are not counted.
Your TMDB API key and self-hosted server address will be deleted from this device, and KevBox Live will go back to the built-in shared service with its daily share.

The built-in service is shared by everyone using KevBox Live. If any minute, hourly or daily allowance is used up, TMDB details pause until that window resets; playlist information keeps working. Your own key or Worker removes this allowance.
KevBox Live Worker · no setup
Leave both blank for KevBox Live’s shared Worker. A custom Worker URL takes priority over a direct API key. Account sessions remain profile-specific.
Send all KevBox Live traffic and playback through an HTTP proxy.
This device does not allow KevBox Live to set exact alarms, so a recording may begin a few minutes late. Recordings start earlier to make up for it.

On any device with a browser on the same Wi-Fi — a phone, a computer or another TV — scan the QR (or open the URL), enter this PIN, choose your KevBox Live backup file and send it. You then pick what to restore here.
KevBox Live could not work out how many channels this provider allows.

Many providers never say how many channels you may watch at the same time, so KevBox Live finds out by opening a few and seeing which ones survive. Anything playing now will stop, and this can take up to two minutes.
Surround — send Dolby/DTS to a real 5.1/7.1 receiver. If it goes silent or stutters, KevBox Live still falls back to stereo and tells you.
KevBox Live plays the playlist your admin sets up for you.
KevBox Live is a media player. It includes no channels or content of its own. Your playlist is set up by the admin, so there is no source for you to add.
